name: Pinar de Chamartin
etymology_summary: Named after a pine grove ('pinar') near the Chamartin area. 'Chamartin' etymology debated: possibly Basque 'ecta-Martin' (village of captain Martin) or French 'Chez Martin'. Interchange with Metro lines 1 and 4.
named_after: Pinar de Chamartin (pine grove near Chamartin area)

name: Fuente de la Mora
etymology_summary: Named after the old Camino Fuente de la Mora. 'Fuente' = spring; 'Mora' may derive from pre-Roman 'mor-' (stones). Shared with Cercanias C-1. Originally planned as 'Manoteras'.
named_after: Fuente de la Mora (spring, from pre-Roman mor-: stones)
source: Garcia Sanchez CVC Rinconete Part IV (cvc.cervantes.es/el_rinconete/anteriores/enero_08/28012008_01.htm); comunidad.madrid/cultura/patrimonio-cultural/yacimiento-arqueologico-fuente-mora

name: Virgen del Cortijo
etymology_summary: Named after the Virgen del Cortijo neighbourhood (1966 development). The name refers to a devotion to the Virgin Mary associated with a local farmstead ('cortijo').
named_after: Virgen del Cortijo neighbourhood (Virgin Mary of the farmstead)

name: Antonio Saura
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Antonio Saura Atares (1930-1998), a major Spanish painter of the post-war period. Co-founder of the El Paso group (1957). Known for expressionist abstract works in black and grey tones.
named_after: Antonio Saura

name: Alvarez de Villaamil
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Jenaro Perez Villaamil y Duguet (1807-1854), the great Spanish romantic landscape painter. He introduced landscape genre painting in Spain and created 'Espana artistica y monumental'.
named_after: Jenaro Perez Villaamil

name: Blasco Ibanez
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Vicente Blasco Ibanez (1867-1928), Valencian novelist, journalist, and politician. Author of 'Los cuatro jinetes del Apocalipsis' and 'Sangre y arena', both adapted by Hollywood.
named_after: Vicente Blasco Ibanez

name: Maria Tudor
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Mary Tudor / Maria I of England (1516-1558). First queen regnant of England. Wife of Felipe II of Spain. Daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon (daughter of the Reyes Catolicos).
named_after: Maria I de Inglaterra

name: Palas de Rey
etymology_summary: Named after the street, which references Palas de Rei, a municipality in Lugo (Galicia) on the Camino de Santiago. From Latin 'Palatium Regis' (Palace of the King), linked to the Visigothic King Witiza (702-710).
named_after: Palas de Rei

name: Las Tablas
etymology_summary: Named after the Las Tablas PAU (new urban development, built early 2000s). 'Tablas' means 'boards/planks' but in agricultural context refers to flat, rectangular land plots.
named_after: Las Tablas neighbourhood (tablas: flat terrain plots)

name: Colonia Jardin
etymology_summary: Named after the 'Colonia Jardin' (garden colony), a planned neighbourhood inspired by the English Garden City movement of Ebenezer Howard and the Linear City of Arturo Soria. These 'colonias' emerged around 1915-1924. Interchange with Metro line 10.
named_after: Colonia Jardin (garden city neighbourhood, early 20th-century urban planning model)

name: Prado de la Vega
etymology_summary: Named after the local area. 'Prado' means 'meadow'; 'de la Vega' means 'of the fertile plain'. Describes the former agricultural landscape of the area.
named_after: Prado de la Vega (meadow of the fertile plain)
source: RAE (dle.rae.es/prado; dle.rae.es/vega); soloboadilla.es (Visigoth settlement 'La Vega'); es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estacion_de_Prado_de_la_Vega; Ayto. Boadilla del Monte

name: Colonia de los Angeles
etymology_summary: Named after the residential colony 'Colonia de los Angeles' (Colony of the Angels), a planned suburban development in Pozuelo de Alarcon.
named_after: Colonia de los Angeles (neighbourhood near Cerro de los Angeles)
source: asoclosangeles.org/colonia-los-angeles (founded 1926); pozuelodealarcon.org/tu-ayuntamiento/tu-ciudad/acerca-de-pozuelo/historia; archimadrid.org (patrona Nuestra Senora de los Angeles); Ayto. Boadilla del Monte

name: Prado del Rey
etymology_summary: Named after the Prado del Rey area. 'Prado del Rey' means 'the King's Meadow' (from Latin pratum: meadow), indicating a royal meadow or pasture belonging to the Crown. The area was historically part of royal hunting grounds. The Arroyo Prado del Rey still flows through the area. The site later became the headquarters of RTVE (state television) from 1964, making 'Prado del Rey' synonymous with Spanish public broadcasting.
named_after: Prado del Rey (the King's Meadow, royal pastureland)
source: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prado_del_Rey; Mesa del Arbol de Carabanchel; La Cerca

name: Somosaguas Sur
etymology_summary: Named after the Somosaguas area in Pozuelo de Alarcon. 'Somosaguas' is a compound of 'somo' (from Latin summum: the highest part, elevated area) + 'aguas' (waters), referring to elevated terrain with water sources. The area historically had ferruginous springs. The hamlet of San Juan de Somosaguas was depopulated during the fratricidal wars between Pedro I and Enrique II (14th century).
named_after: Somosaguas (elevated terrain with springs, from Latin summum + aguas)
source: es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somosaguas; El Correo de Pozuelo; Grupo Abrasador

name: Somosaguas Centro
etymology_summary: Named after central Somosaguas. See Somosaguas Sur for etymology. The area is known for luxury residential urbanizations established from the mid-20th century.
named_after: Somosaguas (elevated terrain with springs, from Latin summum + aguas)

name: Pozuelo Oeste
etymology_summary: Named for its location in the western part of Pozuelo de Alarcon. See Cercanias Pozuelo entry for municipality etymology.
named_after: Pozuelo de Alarcon west (Latin puteolu: small well/spring)

name: Belgica
etymology_summary: Named after the street Calle Belgica (Belgium). Part of a European country-themed street naming pattern in this area of Pozuelo de Alarcon, reflecting European integration themes.
named_after: Belgium

name: Dos Castillas
etymology_summary: Named after the Via de las Dos Castillas street. 'Dos Castillas' (Two Castiles) refers to the historical kingdoms of Castilla la Vieja and Castilla la Nueva, reflecting the area's location within the Castilian heartland.
named_after: Calle Dos Castillas (Two Castiles: Castile and Leon + Castile-La Mancha)

name: Campus de Somosaguas
etymology_summary: Named after the Complutense University campus at Somosaguas, which houses the Faculty of Political Sciences, Economics, Psychology, and Social Work.
named_after: Universidad Complutense de Madrid

name: Avenida de Europa
etymology_summary: Named after the Avenida de Europa (Avenue of Europe), a major urban road through Pozuelo de Alarcon. Reflects European-themed naming in the area's modern urban developments from the 1980s-90s.
named_after: Avenida de Europa (Pozuelo de Alarcon)

name: Berna
etymology_summary: Named after the street Calle Berna (Bern), the capital of Switzerland. Part of the European capitals/countries street naming theme in this area of Pozuelo de Alarcon.
named_after: Bern

name: Estacion de Aravaca
etymology_summary: Terminal station connecting to Cercanias. Named after the Aravaca district, of possible Celtic origin. Documented since Alfonso VIII's fuero (1222). Annexed to Madrid 1951.
named_after: Aravaca

name: Ciudad de la Imagen
etymology_summary: Named after the Ciudad de la Imagen (City of the Image) business park, a complex specializing in audiovisual industries. Home to Telemadrid, ECAM, Filmoteca Espanola, and many production companies.
named_after: Ciudad de la Imagen (audiovisual business park in Pozuelo)

name: Jose Isbert
etymology_summary: Named after Jose Ysbert Alvarruiz 'Pepe Isbert' (1886-1966), legendary Spanish actor. Star of classics like 'Bienvenido Mister Marshall' and 'El verdugo'. Station located near the Filmoteca Nacional in Ciudad de la Imagen.
named_after: Jose Isbert

name: Ciudad del Cine
etymology_summary: Named for its location near the Kinepolis multiplex cinema in the Ciudad de la Imagen area. 'Ciudad del Cine' = 'City of Cinema', reflecting the audiovisual theme of the development.
named_after: Ciudad del Cine (Cinema City, Boadilla del Monte film facilities area)

name: Cocheras
etymology_summary: Named after the Metro Ligero vehicle depot ('cocheras' = depots/garages) located at this station.
named_after: Cocheras (tram/light rail depot and maintenance facility)

name: Retamares
etymology_summary: Named after the Retamares area. From 'retama' (broom plant, Arabic 'ratama') + collective suffix '-es'. 'Place of broom bushes'. The area also hosts the Spanish Ministry of Defence's Estado Mayor de la Defensa.
named_after: Retamares (retamar: place of broom plants, Retama sphaerocarpa)
source: RAE (dle.rae.es/retama -- Arabic ratama); etimologias.dechile.net/?retama; es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estacion_de_Retamares; Ayto. Boadilla del Monte

name: Monteprincipe
etymology_summary: Named after the Monte Principe residential urbanization. The land was part of the Monte de Boadilla, owned from 1761 by Infante Luis Antonio de Borbon. Through inheritance it passed to Carlota Luisa Godoy y Borbon, who married Camilo Ruspoli, Principe de Cerveteri. The Ruspoli family owned the estate until the 1960s-2000s. The name combines 'Monte' (the Boadilla woodland) with the princely title of its Ruspoli owners.
named_after: Monteprincipe (residential development, CEU San Pablo University campus)

name: Ventorro del Cano
etymology_summary: Named after the Ventorro del Cano area in Alcorcon. 'Ventorro' is a diminutive of 'venta' (inn/tavern from Latin vendita), a small roadside establishment for travelers. 'Del Cano' is the surname of the innkeeper. Historically a stopping point (parada de postas) on the old Camino de Extremadura, documented as existing until at least 1828.
named_after: Ventorro del Cano (Cano's roadside inn on the Camino de Extremadura)

name: Prado del Espino
etymology_summary: Named after the Prado del Espino business park and area. 'Prado' = meadow; 'del Espino' = of the hawthorn/thornbush. Describes a historical meadow with hawthorn vegetation.
named_after: Prado del Espino (meadow of the hawthorn, from Latin pratum + spinus)

name: Cantabria
etymology_summary: Named after the Avenida de Cantabria street. Cantabria is a northern Spanish region. The street follows a theme of Spanish regions/geography names in the Boadilla area.
named_after: Cantabria

name: Ferial de Boadilla
etymology_summary: Named after the Boadilla fairground area ('ferial' = fairground/exhibition site). 'De Boadilla' specifies the municipality.
named_after: Ferial de Boadilla (fairground/exhibition area of Boadilla del Monte)

name: Boadilla Centro
etymology_summary: Named for its central location in Boadilla del Monte. The municipality name derives from 'Bobadilla', diminutive of 'Bobada' = 'place for grazing/passage of oxen' (from Latin 'bos/bovis').
named_after: Boadilla del Monte

name: Nuevo Mundo
etymology_summary: Named after a street in Boadilla. 'Nuevo Mundo' = 'New World'. References the Age of Discovery and the Americas, following a historical/geographic naming theme in the development.
named_after: Calle Nuevo Mundo (New World, Americas reference in Boadilla del Monte)

name: Siglo XXI
etymology_summary: Named after the street Calle Siglo XXI ('21st Century Street'). Reflects the modern, forward-looking character of this new residential development in Boadilla.
named_after: Siglo XXI development (21st Century, modern residential area in Boadilla)

name: Infante Don Luis
etymology_summary: Named after the Infante Luis Antonio de Borbon y Farnesio (1727-1785), youngest son of King Felipe V and brother of Carlos III. He acquired the lordship of Boadilla in 1761 and commissioned the neoclassical palace (1763-1765) designed by Ventura Rodriguez.
named_after: Luis Antonio de Borbon y Farnesio

name: Puerta de Boadilla
etymology_summary: Terminal station. 'Puerta de Boadilla' = 'Gateway to Boadilla del Monte'. Serves as the main entrance point to the municipality from the Metro Ligero network.
named_after: Boadilla del Monte
source: Toponomasticon Hispaniae (toponhisp.org/es/toponimia-de-las-zonas-central-sur-e-insular-atlantica/toponimo/boadilla-del-monte); es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estacion_de_Puerta_de_Boadilla; Ayto. Boadilla del Monte

name: Plaza de Toros
etymology_summary: Named after the Parla bullring. 'Plaza de toros' (bullring) is a transparent compound: the station serves the area near Parla's bullring.
named_after: Plaza de Toros de Parla (bullring)

name: Julio Romero de Torres
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Julio Romero de Torres (1874-1930), Spanish painter from Cordoba known for deeply Spanish symbolist art. Professor at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando.
named_after: Julio Romero de Torres

name: La Ballena
etymology_summary: Named after the La Ballena neighbourhood in Parla. The name derives from a popular legend: a large natural lagoon existed in northern Parla (now the 'La Laguna' neighbourhood), and a muleteer threw his 'albarda' (pack saddle) into the water, where it floated resembling a whale's back. Residents of Getafe came to 'fish the whale'. A folk copla mocks this event. The Parque de la Ballena (built 2000) features a giant metal whale tail sculpture. The whale has become one of Parla's municipal symbols.
named_after: La Ballena (folk legend of whale sighting in Parla's lagoon)
source: leyendasmundialesmagicas.blogspot.com/2017/12/una-ballena-parla-madrid.html; Raul Cordero 'La ciudad de la ballena'; esculturayarte.com/007314/Cola-de-Ballena-en-Parla.html; es.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Ballena_(Parla)

name: Parla Centro-Bulevar Norte
etymology_summary: 'Parla Centro' indicates the town centre location. 'Bulevar Norte' refers to the northern boulevard. The municipality name has debated etymology: Roman anthroponym 'Parilus', Latin 'parabola' (speech), or folk legend of a mute woman who began to 'parlar'.
named_after: Parla town centre + Bulevar Norte (northern boulevard)

name: Iglesia Centro
etymology_summary: Named for its proximity to the central parish church ('iglesia') of Parla, the Iglesia de Nuestra Senora de la Asuncion.
named_after: Iglesia de Nuestra Senora de la Asuncion (Parla parish church)

name: Bulevar Sur-Miguel Angel Blanco
etymology_summary: 'Bulevar Sur' = Southern Boulevard. 'Miguel Angel Blanco' (1968-1997) was a PP councillor in Ermua (Basque Country) kidnapped and murdered by ETA. Streets across Spain were named in his honour as a symbol of resistance against terrorism.
named_after: Miguel Angel Blanco

name: Reyes Catolicos
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring the Reyes Catolicos (Catholic Monarchs): Queen Isabel I of Castile (1451-1504) and King Fernando II of Aragon (1452-1516), who unified Spain and sponsored Columbus's voyage.
named_after: Reyes Catolicos

name: Isabel II
etymology_summary: Named after the street honouring Queen Isabel II of Spain (1830-1904), who reigned 1833-1868. Under her reign, major railway construction was undertaken in Spain including the Madrid-Aranjuez line.
named_after: Isabel II de Espana

name: Parque Parla Este
etymology_summary: Named after the park ('parque') in the eastern ('este') part of Parla.
named_after: Parque Parla Este (eastern park of Parla)

name: Avenida Sistema Solar
etymology_summary: Named after the Avenida del Sistema Solar (Solar System Avenue). Part of an astronomy/space-themed street naming pattern in the Parla Este new development, with streets named after planets and celestial features.
named_after: Avenida del Sistema Solar (Solar System Avenue, astronomical theme in Parla Este)

name: Tierra
etymology_summary: Named after the Calle Tierra (Earth Street). Part of the solar system/astronomy naming theme in the Parla Este development. Dual station (serves both directions of circular line).
named_after: Planet Earth (astronomical theme in Parla Este Tranvia)

name: Venus
etymology_summary: Named after the Calle Venus (Venus Street), referencing the planet. Part of the solar system naming theme. Dual station.
named_after: Planet Venus (astronomical theme in Parla Este Tranvia)

name: Estrella Polar
etymology_summary: Named after the Calle Estrella Polar (Polaris/North Star Street). Part of the astronomical naming theme. Dual station.
named_after: Polaris / North Star (astronomical theme in Parla Este Tranvia)

name: Jaime I
etymology_summary: Named after the Calle Jaime I. Jaime I 'el Conquistador' (1208-1276) was King of Aragon who conquered the Balearic Islands, Valencia, and Murcia. Dual station.
named_after: Jaime I de Aragon

name: Poligono Industrial Ciudad de Parla
etymology_summary: Named after Parla's main industrial park ('poligono industrial'). The term refers to the planned industrial zone of the municipality.
named_after: Poligono Industrial Ciudad de Parla (Parla industrial estate)
